text:
maria-support: FYI, customer 'Flicker' reporting bursts of 429 + high p99 latency hitting their Dedicated pool this morning around 08:12 UTC. Requests queue then 429s. :eyes:

alex-eng-runtime: Can you paste the request IDs / sample logs? Is this the dedicated pool with min_replicas=2?

maria-support: Yep min=2 max=20 on eu-west. Sample request IDs: req_2f9c, req_2fa1. Logs attached (snippet):
```
2026-03-16T08:12:03Z scale-controller: desired_replicas=6 current=2 reason=latency_spike
2026-03-16T08:12:06Z provisioner: provisioning node n-gpu-17 status=pending
2026-03-16T08:12:30Z kube: pod scheduling backoff: waiting for resources (gpu-0)
2026-03-16T08:13:12Z runtime: request req_2f9c queued, queue_len=72
2026-03-16T08:13:45Z runtime: respond 429 client=customer-flicker reason=throttled_queue
```

sam-eng-infra: That looks like slow node provisioning + pod schedule backoff. Any cloud quota events? ops-bot: quota-check returned OK for GPUs in eu-west.

linda-eng-sre: Also check noisy neighbor — one existing node had repeated container OOMs earlier, could be eviction thrash that slows scheduler. Any node-level logs?

maria-support: I grabbed kube events from the pool: `FailedScheduling: insufficient resource: nvidia.com/gpu` and one node with status: "NotReady: Kubelet - OOMKill" around 08:05.

alex-eng-runtime: Two failure modes we see often: autoscaler only scales when CPU/latency metric crosses threshold, but requests can pile in if prefix caching misses and each request is heavy. If provisioning latency per replica ~60-90s, min=2 -> cold start window causes queue/429s.

maria-support: Customer says problem started after they changed model to longer context (more memory). Could explain OOMs.

sam-eng-infra: Quick mitigations for the customer: 1) increase min_replicas to 4 temporarily 2) enable burst_capacity (if available) 3) add warmup jobs to keep KV cache alive.

linda-eng-sre: Also recommend changing scale policy: allow scale_up_step to >1 (e.g., scale_up_increment: 3) and reduce cool_down window to let autoscaler react faster. For Dedicated, we can bump the initial provisioning parallelism flag.

maria-support: I'll propose min=4 and scale_up_increment=3 to the customer. Any objections? :thumbsup: 

alex-eng-runtime: No objections. Also filing infra task to look at scheduler logs and node image compatibility w/ new model. Might be a tensorRT driver mismatch causing container restarts.

sam-eng-infra: Created infra ticket INF-4219 to investigate OOM/Ops patterns and provisioning parallelism. Adding customer request IDs and cluster events.

maria-support: Customer approved temporary min increase. Applied change at 08:28 UTC. Monitoring now.

ops-bot: deploy-change: updated pool flicker-dedicated min_replicas: 2 -> 4 by maria-support at 2026-03-16T08:28:10Z

maria-support: After change, queue dropped to <10 and 429s stopped by 08:34. They still saw a single 503 due to one node eviction.

linda-eng-sre: Followups: 1) confirm node driver compatibility with model image 2) recommend customer evaluate model quantization to reduce memory 3) enable autoscaler metric for queue_length not just CPU/latency.

alex-eng-runtime: I'll add a patch to the autoscaler to include request_queue_len as a trigger option (RFC in eng-runtime backlog).

maria-support: Marking customer case updated, they are unblocked for now. Will keep open until infra confirms root cause. :white_check_mark:

sam-eng-infra: Noted. INF-4219 owner: sam-eng-infra. ETA initial findings EOD.

linda-eng-sre: If we see recurrence, we should consider offering a short 'warm pool' addon for Dedicated customers with high cold-start sensitivity.

maria-support: Thanks team. Closing initial support thread; will re-open if infra finds anything actionable.
